data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English ‘rosa monde’, meaning ‘rose strength’. Rosamond was a popular name among the English nobility in the Middle Ages, and was often given to girls born during the month of May. The name Rosamond carries the meaning “rose, strength” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Rosamond usually hope their child will grow to embody rose, strength and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Rosamond was a character in the 18th-century legend of the "Fair Rosamond," who was said to have been a beautiful and alluring woman who captivated King Henry I of England. The legend tells of a love triangle between Rosamond, the king, and the courtier Sir Willibald, which ultimately led to Rosamond's tragic death. The story was popularized in poetry, art, and literature, and Rosamond became a symbol of forbidden love and desire.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Rosamond can be seen as a reminder of the strength and beauty of the rose, a symbol of love, compassion, and the Divine in many spiritual traditions. Rosamond's story can serve as a reminder of the dangers of passion and desire unchecked, as well as the power of love and its ability to transcend human limitations. It can also invoke the image of the Virgin Mary, whose name means 'full of grace' and is often associated with roses. Thus, the name Rosamond can be seen as a reminder of the dual nature of love- its capacity for both joy and sorrow, and its potential to bring us closer to the Divine.
